paragraphs: R' Patya Ukhma. Megillah 14, end of b: Rav Nahman said. Rav Eina the Elder raised an objection to Rav Nahman, etc. He told him, ‘Eina the Elder’—some say, ‘Patya Ukhma’—‘between me and you the matter will be completed’; Pesahim 88a. Berakhot 50a: Rava called Rafram bar Pappa ‘Patya Ukhma.’ In Avodah Zarah 16b, Rav Assi called R' Zeira ‘Patya Ukhma.’ See Arukh, entry פתיא: the meaning is ‘black vessel.’ Hiddushei Aggadot on Megillah writes that he intended praise rather than disparagement, as they say in Ta'anit, ‘Splendid wisdom in an ugly vessel,’ etc., and ‘Had they been ugly, they would have learned more.’ Shalshelet Ha-Kabbalah 35a writes, citing Yalkut on 2 Kings 22 (remez 248:1), concerning the matter mentioned in Megillah, etc., that he was a black man, short and small, about a handbreadth, and wise; he lived close to the time of Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak.
